text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An influx of brown locusts threatens large tracts of regions on the edge of the Kalahari desert, according to the Namibian Early Warning and Food Information System. The agriculture ministry is setting up 105 teams to deal with the locusts.
- Singaporean Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and a 30-member delegation are expected in Namibia for a three-day visit aimed at promoting ties, particularly in Namibia's Export Processing Zone.
- Academic Joseph Diescho called at a seminar in Namibia for African intellectuals not to collaborate with official lies and to make ordinary people aware of their circumstances.
